```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2026_anakinra"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2026_anakinra"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70491> (open access; the
  supporting information holds the NONMEM control stream of the final model)
* Trial protocol: Green EA et al., Front Immunol 2022;13:1022104,
  <https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2022.1022104>

# Population

Li 2026 analysed 25 extremely preterm neonates (born 24 weeks 0 days to
27 weeks 6 days gestation; median gestational age 26.3 weeks) from the
Anakinra Pilot Phase I/IIa trial (NCT05280340) at Monash Children's Hospital,
Melbourne (19 neonates) and Starship Children's Hospital, Auckland (6). All
received intravenous anakinra from birth for 21 days: stage 1, 1.0 mg/kg every
48 h (n = 9); stage 2, 0.8 mg/kg every 24 h (n = 16). Baseline body weight was
0.90 kg (median; range 0.54-1.30) and changed little over therapy
(0.53-1.60 kg); 60% were female (Table 1). 178 samples (4-8 per neonate)
were measured with an AlphaLISA immunoassay that does not separate anakinra
from endogenous IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra), so every measured
concentration is the sum of the two; the observed baseline endogenous IL-1Ra
was 8,755 pg/mL (median; 295-87,100).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Li_2026_anakinra")()$population`.

# Source trace

The final estimates are in Table 2 and Eq. 6-7; the supplement's NONMEM
control stream carries the same values in `$THETA` and the variances behind
Table 2's IIV and residual standard deviations in `$OMEGA` / `$SIGMA`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL, mature, 70 kg) | log(3.97 L/h) | Table 2 'CL'; Eq. 6; ctl THETA(1) |
| `lvc` (V, 70 kg) | log(28.9 L) | Table 2 'V'; Eq. 7; ctl THETA(2) |
| `lbl_il1ra` (endogenous baseline) | log(0.00664 mg/L) = 6,640 pg/mL | Table 2 'BSL'; ctl THETA(3); `IPRED = F + BSL` |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.75, 1 (fixed) | Table 2; Methods (theory-based allometry) |
| `cl_pna_famp` | -0.554 (= -FCL) | Table 2 'FCL' 0.55; Eq. 6; ctl THETA(4) 0.554 |
| `lcl_pna_kdes` | log(ln 2 / 1.80 day) | Table 2 'PNAT50'; Eq. 3 and 6; ctl THETA(5) |
| `limax`, `lic50` | log(1), log(0.04 mg/L) (fixed) | Eq. 5 (assumed, from literature) |
| `etalcl` | 0.0798 | ctl `$OMEGA`; Table 2 'IIV CL' 0.28 = sqrt(0.0798) |
| `etalbl_il1ra` | 0.898 | ctl `$OMEGA`; Table 2 'IIV BSL' 0.95 = sqrt(0.898) |
| IIV on V | omitted | ctl `$OMEGA 0 FIX`; Results (not identifiable) |
| `propSd` | 0.765 | ctl `$SIGMA` 0.585 (variance); Table 2 'Proportional error' 0.77 |
| CL = CL70 (WT/70)^0.75 (1 - FCL exp(-ln2 PNA/PNAT50)) | n/a | Eq. 3 and 6; ctl `FPNA_CL`, `TVCL` |
| V = V70 (WT/70) | n/a | Eq. 7; ctl `TVV` |
| Cc = A/V + BSL, proportional error | n/a | Methods; ctl `$ERROR` |
| inhibition = Imax C / (IC50 + C) | n/a | Eq. 5 |

# Typical-value checks

The abstract and Results quote typical values for a 0.9 kg neonate and the
fraction of mature clearance at birth and by day 10. These do not depend on
any random draw, so they are checked tightly.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Li_2026_anakinra")
days_per_month <- 30.4375

typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod),
  events = data.frame(
    id = 1, time = c(0, 1, 2), evid = 0, cmt = "central",
    WT = 0.9, PNA = c(0, 10, 1000) / days_per_month
  ),
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
typ_tab <- data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "CL at birth / mature CL", "CL at PNA day 10 / mature CL",
    "Mature CL, 0.9 kg (L/h)", "V, 0.9 kg (L)",
    "Inhibition from the endogenous baseline alone"
  ),
  paper = c(0.446, 1.00, 0.15, 0.37, 0.15),
  model = c(
    typ$cl[1] / typ$cl[3], typ$cl[2] / typ$cl[3], typ$cl[3], typ$vc[1],
    typ$inhib[1]
  )
)
knitr::kable(
  typ_tab |> dplyr::rename("Quantity" = quantity, "Li 2026" = paper, "Model" = model),
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste(
    "Typical values. Paper values: Results ('44.6%'), Results and abstract",
    "('~100% by day 10', '0.15 L/h/0.9 kg', '0.37 .../0.9 kg') and the t = 0",
    "inhibition read from Figure 3b/3d."
  )
)
stopifnot(
  abs(typ$cl[1] / typ$cl[3] - 0.446) < 0.001,
  typ$cl[2] / typ$cl[3] > 0.98,
  abs(typ$cl[3] - 0.15) < 0.005,
  abs(typ$vc[1] - 0.37) < 0.005,
  abs(typ$inhib[1] - 0.142) < 0.002
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The authors simulated 1,000 neonates per regimen with demographics resampled
from the trial. Here 200 neonates per regimen have body weight drawn from a
log-normal distribution around the trial median (0.9 kg, about 25% CV),
truncated to the observed baseline range 0.54-1.30 kg and held constant, as
Table 1 shows little change in weight over therapy. Dosing starts at birth
(PNA 0), as in the authors' simulations.

Postnatal age advances in whole days (day of life: 0 throughout the first 24 h,
1 throughout the next, and so on). This is how the trial dataset records PNA
(Table 1: 'Postnatal age (days) 0-20'), and it is the encoding that
reproduces the authors' Figure 4; the sensitivity section below shows what a
continuously advancing PNA changes.

```{r cohort}
inf_dur <- 5 / 60 # short infusion; the duration is not reported

regimen_doses <- function(regimen) {
  q12 <- data.frame(time = seq(0, 498, by = 12))
  q12$day <- q12$time %/% 24
  switch(
    regimen,
    "Stage 1" = data.frame(time = seq(0, 480, by = 48), mgkg = 1.0),
    "Stage 2" = data.frame(time = seq(0, 480, by = 24), mgkg = 0.8),
    "R1" = q12 |>
      mutate(mgkg = case_when(day <= 1 ~ 0.4, day == 2 ~ 0.6, day <= 5 ~ 1.2, TRUE ~ 1.8)),
    "R2" = q12 |>
      mutate(mgkg = case_when(day == 0 ~ 0.6, day == 1 ~ 0.8, day <= 3 ~ 1.0, TRUE ~ 1.3)),
    "R3" = q12 |>
      mutate(mgkg = case_when(day == 0 ~ 0.6, day == 1 ~ 0.8, day <= 3 ~ 1.0, TRUE ~ 1.15)),
    "0.8 mg/kg q24h" = data.frame(time = seq(0, 72, by = 24), mgkg = 0.8),
    "0.4 mg/kg q12h" = data.frame(time = seq(0, 84, by = 12), mgkg = 0.4)
  ) |>
    dplyr::select(time, mgkg)
}

draw_weights <- function(n) {
  wt <- numeric(0)
  while (length(wt) < n) {
    w <- exp(rnorm(n, log(0.9), 0.25))
    wt <- c(wt, w[w >= 0.54 & w <= 1.30])
  }
  wt[seq_len(n)]
}

# One record per hour plus the end of every infusion. PNA is the day of life
# by default; pna_continuous = TRUE advances it with every record instead.
make_cohort <- function(n, regimen, id_offset, t_end = 504, pna_continuous = FALSE,
                        wt = draw_weights(n)) {
  doses <- regimen_doses(regimen)
  subj <- data.frame(id = id_offset + seq_len(n), WT = wt)
  obs_t <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, t_end, by = 1), doses$time + inf_dur)))
  dose_rows <- merge(subj, doses) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = mgkg * WT, dur = inf_dur) |>
    select(-mgkg)
  obs_rows <- merge(subj, data.frame(time = obs_t)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, dur = NA_real_)
  pna_days <- function(time) if (pna_continuous) time / 24 else floor(time / 24)
  bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    mutate(
      regimen = regimen,
      cmt = "central",
      PNA = pna_days(time) / days_per_month
    ) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

set.seed(2026)
n_arm <- 200L
# The same body weights in every regimen, so differences between regimens
# come from the dosing and not from which neonates each arm happened to draw.
cohort_wt <- draw_weights(n_arm)
regimens <- c("Stage 1", "Stage 2", "R1", "R2", "R3")
events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(regimens), function(i) {
  make_cohort(n_arm, regimens[i], id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_arm, wt = cohort_wt)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

PNA and weight are carried on every record, each holding from that record
onward (`covsInterpolation = "locf"`).

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("regimen", "WT"),
  covsInterpolation = "locf",
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  # Late in a 48 h dosing gap the solved concentration wanders around zero
  # at the 1e-8 mg/L level; a negative value there breaks PKNCA's log-down AUC.
  mutate(C_anakinra = pmax(central / vc, 0))
```

`Cc` is the model's prediction of what the assay measures (anakinra plus
endogenous IL-1Ra); `C_anakinra` removes the endogenous baseline and is used
for the exposure (AUC) calculations below. The baseline adds about
0.16 mg*h/L per day, about 1% of the target exposure.

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 3: concentration and inhibition over the first 96 h

```{r figure-3}
events_f3 <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(200L, "0.8 mg/kg q24h", id_offset = 0L, t_end = 96),
  make_cohort(200L, "0.4 mg/kg q12h", id_offset = 200L, t_end = 96)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_f3[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
sim_f3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events_f3,
  keep = "regimen",
  covsInterpolation = "locf",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)

f3 <- sim_f3 |>
  select(regimen, time, Cc, inhib) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, inhib), names_to = "output", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(regimen, output, time) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(value, 0.025),
    med = median(value),
    hi = quantile(value, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(output = ifelse(output == "Cc", "Concentration (mg/L)", "Inhibition (fraction)"))

ref_lines <- data.frame(
  output = c("Concentration (mg/L)", "Inhibition (fraction)"),
  y = c(0.04, 0.5)
)
ggplot(f3, aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(data = ref_lines, aes(yintercept = y), linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkred") +
  facet_grid(output ~ regimen, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 96, by = 24)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Li 2026: median and 95% prediction interval."
  )
```

The figure's medians, read by eye, are compared below: the concentration one
hour after the first 0.8 mg/kg dose, and the trough inhibition before the
second, third and fourth doses.

```{r figure-3-check}
f3_check <- sim_f3 |>
  filter(
    (regimen == "0.8 mg/kg q24h" & time %in% c(1, 24, 48, 72)) |
      (regimen == "0.4 mg/kg q12h" & time %in% c(48, 60, 84))
  ) |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(Cc = median(Cc), inhib = median(inhib), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    output = ifelse(time == 1, "Cc", "inhib"),
    simulated = ifelse(output == "Cc", Cc, inhib)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~regimen, ~time, ~figure3,
      "0.8 mg/kg q24h", 1, 1.63,
      "0.8 mg/kg q24h", 24, 0.46,
      "0.8 mg/kg q24h", 48, 0.27,
      "0.8 mg/kg q24h", 72, 0.21,
      "0.4 mg/kg q12h", 48, 0.59,
      "0.4 mg/kg q12h", 60, 0.49,
      "0.4 mg/kg q12h", 84, 0.41
    ),
    by = c("regimen", "time")
  ) |>
  select(regimen, time, output, figure3, simulated)
knitr::kable(
  f3_check |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Regimen" = regimen, "Time (h)" = time, "Output" = output,
      "Figure 3 median" = figure3, "Simulated median" = simulated
    ),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Figure 3 medians (Cc in mg/L at 1 h; inhibition fraction just before a dose)."
)
stopifnot(
  abs(f3_check$simulated[f3_check$output == "Cc"] / 1.63 - 1) < 0.1,
  all(abs(f3_check$simulated[f3_check$output == "inhib"] -
    f3_check$figure3[f3_check$output == "inhib"]) < 0.1)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper's exposure metric is the AUC over each postnatal day (AUC0-24h,
Figures 2 and 4). PKNCA computes it per day and regimen from the anakinra-only
concentration. For the every-48-hour stage 1 regimen the AUC is computed over
each 48 h dosing interval and halved: the stage 1 boxes in Figure 2 appear only
on even days and sit at about half the AUC that a 1.0 mg/kg dose produces in a
day, so they are read as the average daily AUC.

```{r pknca}
nca_in <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(C_anakinra)) |>
  select(id, regimen, time, C_anakinra)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, regimen, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_in, C_anakinra ~ time | regimen + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id)

intervals <- bind_rows(
  merge(
    data.frame(regimen = c("Stage 2", "R1", "R2", "R3")),
    data.frame(start = (0:20) * 24, end = (1:21) * 24)
  ),
  data.frame(regimen = "Stage 1", start = seq(0, 480, by = 48)) |>
    mutate(end = pmin(start + 48, 504))
) |>
  mutate(auclast = TRUE)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

auc_day <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  mutate(
    day = start / 24,
    auc24 = ifelse(regimen == "Stage 1", PPORRES * 24 / (end - start), PPORRES)
  )
```

## Figure 4: exposure under the proposed regimens

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
auc_day |>
  filter(regimen %in% c("R1", "R2", "R3")) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(day), auc24)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, coef = 1e6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 9.6, linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkred") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 30, linetype = "dashed", colour = "navy") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15, 20)) +
  labs(
    x = "Postnatal age (days)", y = "AUC0-24h (mg*h/L)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 4 of Li 2026; whiskers span the full range.",
      "Dashed lines: target 9.6 and safety limit 30 mg*h/L."
    )
  )
```

## Figure 2: exposure under the trial regimens

```{r figure-2}
auc_day |>
  filter(regimen %in% c("Stage 1", "Stage 2")) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(day), auc24, fill = regimen)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, coef = 1e6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 9.6, linetype = "dashed", colour = "darkred") +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = seq(0, 20, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Postnatal age (days)", y = "AUC0-24h (mg*h/L)", fill = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Compare Figure 2 of Li 2026 (post hoc exposures of the trial",
      "neonates); here a virtual cohort dosed from birth."
    )
  )
```

## Comparison against the published exposures

Figure 4 medians were read by eye by the maintainers (about +/- 0.5
mg*h/L); the stage 2 values are the Results text (9.8 mg*h/L on the day
of birth, a plateau near 4.5 mg*h/L from day 10) and Figure 2.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~day, ~auclast,
  "R1", 0, 10.5, "R1", 1, 7.5, "R1", 2, 9.5, "R1", 3, 17.0,
  "R1", 4, 16.0, "R1", 5, 15.3, "R1", 6, 22.2, "R1", 20, 21.0,
  "R2", 0, 15.8, "R2", 1, 15.0, "R2", 2, 15.8, "R2", 3, 14.2,
  "R2", 4, 17.3, "R2", 5, 16.6, "R2", 6, 16.1, "R2", 20, 15.3,
  "R3", 0, 15.8, "R3", 1, 15.0, "R3", 2, 15.8, "R3", 3, 14.2,
  "R3", 4, 15.3, "R3", 5, 14.7, "R3", 6, 14.3, "R3", 20, 13.5,
  "Stage 2", 0, 9.8, "Stage 2", 10, 4.5, "Stage 2", 20, 4.3
) |>
  mutate(group = paste0(regimen, ", day ", day))

sim_cmp <- auc_day |>
  inner_join(published |> select(regimen, day, group), by = c("regimen", "day")) |>
  transmute(group, PPTESTCD = "auclast", PPORRES = auc24)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_cmp,
  reference = published |> select(group, auclast),
  by = "group",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Median AUC0-24h by postnatal day. * differs from the published value by >20%."
)

fig4_pct <- auc_day |>
  filter(regimen %in% c("R1", "R2", "R3")) |>
  group_by(regimen, day) |>
  summarise(sim = median(auc24), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(published, by = c("regimen", "day")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - auclast) / auclast)
stopifnot(
  # Each regimen's medians move together across days, offset by the IIV draw
  # of its 200 neonates (about +-3% per arm); a mis-transcribed CL, FCL or
  # PNAT50 shifts whole profiles or the first days by 10% or more.
  abs(median(fig4_pct$pct_diff)) < 8,
  quantile(abs(fig4_pct$pct_diff), 0.9) < 15
)
```

The proposed regimens (R1-R3) agree with Figure 4 to within a few percent from
postnatal day 1 onward, including days 1-3, where the change in clearance is
fastest. On the day of birth all three run about 7% below the figure; how the
authors' simulation advanced postnatal age within the first day is not
reported, and the day-0 AUC is the one most sensitive to it (see the
sensitivity section). The stage 2 virtual cohort runs 10-15% above the Results
values: the trial neonates started anakinra within the first 24 h of life
rather than at birth, and Figure 2 summarises their individual post hoc
estimates rather than a simulated population.

## Target attainment

Li 2026 reports that about 95% of neonates reached the 9.6 mg*h/L target
under R2, with 4% above the 30 mg*h/L safety limit, and that R3 cut the
excess-exposure risk ten-fold for a 5% loss of target attainment. The
fraction of neonate-days meeting each bound is shown for reference; the paper
does not state whether its percentages are per day or over the whole course,
so they are not used as a pass/fail check.

```{r attainment}
auc_day |>
  filter(regimen %in% c("R1", "R2", "R3")) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    target = mean(auc24 >= 9.6),
    above_safety = mean(auc24 > 30),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Neonate-days AUC >= 9.6" = target,
    "Neonate-days AUC > 30" = above_safety
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Fraction of simulated neonate-days by exposure bound.")
```

## Sensitivity: continuously advancing postnatal age

Clearance changes fastest in the first days of life, so the AUC there depends
on how PNA is fed to the model. The typical neonate (0.9 kg) under R2 is
solved with PNA as the day of life and with PNA advancing every hour.

```{r pna-sensitivity}
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ_events <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(1L, "R2", id_offset = 0L, wt = 0.9) |>
    mutate(pna_encoding = "day of life"),
  make_cohort(1L, "R2", id_offset = 0L, wt = 0.9, pna_continuous = TRUE) |>
    mutate(pna_encoding = "continuous")
)
# One single-subject solve per encoding (the typical neonate in each).
typ_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(split(typ_events, typ_events$pna_encoding), function(ev) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod_typical,
    events = ev,
    covsInterpolation = "locf",
    returnType = "data.frame"
  ) |>
    # A single-subject solve returns no id column.
    mutate(id = 1L, pna_encoding = ev$pna_encoding[1], C_anakinra = pmax(central / vc, 0))
}))
typ_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
    typ_sim |> select(id, pna_encoding, time, C_anakinra),
    C_anakinra ~ time | pna_encoding + id
  ),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
    typ_events |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, pna_encoding, time, amt),
    amt ~ time | pna_encoding + id
  ),
  intervals = data.frame(start = (0:6) * 24, end = (1:7) * 24, auclast = TRUE)
))
as.data.frame(typ_nca) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  transmute(day = start / 24, pna_encoding, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = pna_encoding, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(pct_change = 100 * (continuous - `day of life`) / `day of life`) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Postnatal day" = day, "AUC, PNA as day of life" = `day of life`,
    "AUC, PNA continuous" = continuous, "Change (%)" = pct_change
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical-neonate AUC0-24h (mg*h/L) under R2.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Postnatal age as day of life.** The model takes PNA in months (the
  register's unit) and converts to days internally. The paper's dataset
  records PNA in whole days, and its simulated exposures (Figure 4) are
  reproduced when PNA is held at the day of life over each day; a
  continuously advancing PNA gives lower exposures over the first days of
  life, as the sensitivity table shows. Users simulating new regimens should
  decide which encoding fits their purpose.
- **Fractional maturation written as a signed amplitude.** The paper's
  `1 - FCL exp(-ln2 PNA / PNAT50)` is encoded as
  `1 + cl_pna_famp exp(-cl_pna_kdes PNA)` with `cl_pna_famp = -FCL` and
  `cl_pna_kdes = ln2 / PNAT50`, the library's form for a postnatal-age
  effect. The two are identical.
- **Final estimates from the control stream.** The supplement's NONMEM
  control stream holds the final estimates (its `$THETA` values equal Table 2
  and Eq. 6), so the variances there are used directly: Table 2's IIV and
  proportional-error entries are their square roots, to the printed rounding.
- **IIV on V omitted.** The control stream fixes it to 0 (Table S1 model 3;
  not identifiable), so the model carries no `etalvc`.
- **Units.** The baseline is reported in pg/mL; the model works in mg and
  mg/L, so 6,640 pg/mL is entered as 0.00664 mg/L. `Cc` includes the
  endogenous baseline, as the assay does; the AUC calculations here subtract
  it.
- **Inhibition model.** Eq. 5 is an assumed direct-effect model (Imax = 1,
  IC50 = 0.04 mg/L, from the literature), not one fitted to neonatal data.
  The paper says it is driven by the concentration predicted by the final
  model; the t = 0 inhibition of about 0.15 in Figure 3b and 3d is what the
  endogenous baseline alone gives, so `inhib` uses `Cc` including the
  baseline.
- **Infusion duration.** Not reported. Doses are given as 5-minute infusions;
  Figure 3a's median one hour after a 0.8 mg/kg dose (1.63 mg/L) matches a
  short infusion.
- **Virtual cohort.** Body weight drawn log-normally around the trial median
  and held constant, the same weights in every regimen; dosing from birth;
  200 neonates per regimen (the authors used 1,000).
- No correction notice for Li 2026 was found as of 2026-11-18.
